message:
Follow-up: implement #842 review notes for publish permission flow

## Summary
This PR applies the follow-up agreed in #842 and the corresponding review thread on the publish flow: run the `publish` permission check against the resolved draft record, rather than before draft resolution.

## Background
In the review on #842, the consensus/LGTM was that permission evaluation for publish should use the same concrete record context as the rest of the operation. The only remaining implementation detail was to move the check to after draft lookup so the draft can be passed into `require_permission(...)`.

This PR is just the mechanical application of that already-approved direction:
- resolve the draft first
- invoke `require_permission(identity, "publish", record=draft)`
- leave the rest of the publish flow unchanged

## Why this follow-up
This keeps the permission call aligned with the object actually being published and with the review notes from the earlier discussion. It also makes the permission hook consistent with other service methods that evaluate against a concrete record instance.

## Scope
No behavioral changes are intended beyond implementing the previously approved permission-context wiring from #842. Re-litigating whether publish checks should be record-aware was already covered in the prior review; this PR only applies that decision in code.

## Notes
- no schema/API changes
- no changes to the publish transaction itself
- validation and publish semantics remain as-is
